questions.question: Hydroplaning is most like:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a film of water. Your tires lose contact with the road surface, similar to water skiing.

questions.question: If your trailer starts to jackknife, you should NOT:

options.text: Allow the trailer to straighten out.
Allow the wheels to grip the road.

questions.explanation: If your trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels regain grip. Do not use the trailer hand brake—it will make the skid worse. Brakes lock the wheels, which caused the problem in the first place.

questions.question: With a combination vehicle, it is best to:
questions.explanation: Brake well in advance and look far ahead to avoid sudden stops. This habit prevents your trailer from jackknifing.

questions.question: A trailer is most likely to swing around when it is:
questions.explanation: An empty trailer needs a longer stopping distance than a loaded one. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear and use brakes to help slow the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear and use brakes to help slow the engine.
questions.explanation: The engine's braking power should be your main way to control speed downhill. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a driver on the roadside

questions.explanation: Accident scenes are hazardous because people may not watch traffic. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children who may not notice vehicles. Open roads have no hazards.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan how you will respond if danger appears.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, they work:

options.text: Only if a green lever on the panel is pushed.

questions.explanation: Air brakes take a half-second or more to work after you press the pedal. Air must travel through the lines to reach the brakes. Car brakes are hydraulic and work instantly.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase space between you and the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase space between you and the car in front.
questions.explanation: Create more space ahead so the tailgater can safely pass. Speeding up will not help—the driver may just tailgate you faster.

questions.question: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, keep it from moving by:
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks to prevent the trailer from moving. Air brakes only work as long as air pressure stays in the tanks. Wheel chocks ensure the trailer stays safe.

questions.question: What can help you know when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. Engine speed (rpm) is one. Check your vehicle's manual for the right rpm range, then shift up when you reach the top. Road speed (mph) is the other. Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: Starting in what year did new trailers need to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver apply spring brakes slowly. In vehicles that have one, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: Before driving, how do you check that air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for air escaping.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air in the brake system reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build up. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from those valves, air is reaching the whole vehicle.

questions.question: If a trailer's spring brakes won't release when you push the tractor air supply control, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Before you start a trip, all equipment must work correctly. If a trailer's spring brakes don't release when you push the tractor air supply control, check that all air line connections are tight and sealed.

questions.question: When backing up, what is best?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Back up as quickly as possible.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.

questions.explanation: When you must drive in reverse, back up slowly. Use mirrors on both sides of your vehicle. Have a helper watch your blind spots whenever you can. Agree on a signal that means "stop."

questions.question: If you find something unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Continue the trip and see a mechanic after you finish.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Skip using those parts, but drive normally otherwise.

questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you must have it repaired. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The risk of jackknifing is lower.
The risk of jackknifing is higher.
The brakes won't work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risk of jackknifing is lower.
questions.explanation: When the tractor has ABS but the trailer doesn't, jackknifing risk goes down. You can still steer the vehicle. When only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out to one side.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should go off right away. If a light stays on, it usually means there is a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: If you must write out a vehicle inspection report, when must you sign it?

options.text: Only if defects were found and fixed or certified as not needing repair.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a law enforcement officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and fixed or certified as not needing repair.
questions.explanation: You must sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and certified as fixed or not needing to be fixed.
